checks: Read s26_flux_recovery.py: the Fourier-Gaussian convolution to the Xb4f header beam, the beam-area rescaling (valid for smooth emission), the per-pixel line-free baseline, matched apertures and 1-arcsec peak boxes are standard and stated. Agree.

Independent re-derivation (checks/q8_cont.py): I smoothed the Xb4d and Xb4b continuum mfs to the Xb4f continuum beam with a circular-equivalent Gaussian and scaled by beam area. Peak recovery vs Xb4f is Xb4d 0.86 (N) and 0.80 (S), Xb4b 0.76 (N) and 0.65 (S). The worker found 0.84/0.79 and 0.73/0.68. Agree within 3%, so the continuum recovery and the 'line and continuum are filtered alike' claim hold.

The worker's own tables are consistent. The HCO+ peak recovery (0.87/0.81/0.87) matches the continuum, the aperture sums saturate at r~8 arcsec in Xb4f, and the Xb4b r<12 arcsec sum is ~0 (the negative bowl expected without short spacings). The 35-55% resolved-out interpretation follows.

The Xb4b vs Xb4d agreement at the matched 0.94 arcsec beam (0-8%) is a good calibration null test. It shows the Xb4f differences are spatial filtering and not a flux-scale offset. The HCN/HCO+ stability (<=2% N, <=9% S and Bridge) is a useful, physically important result, and the faint-clump (E2, Sblue, W, E1) caveats are called out appropriately.
The CH3OH conclusion is calibrated honestly: ratios 0.7-0.8 +-0.3 and 20-30% resolved out at ~1.5 sigma, not significant individually. Agree that the earlier '1/3 recovery' was beam dilution.
notes_for_questioner: (1) State in the published entry that the 35%/55% resolved-out fractions are lower limits on missing flux relative to Xb4f. Xb4f has no zero-spacing data and could itself miss extended flux, so 'resolved out at 0.24 arcsec' means 'relative to Xb4f'. Compare the Xb4f HCO+/HCN 3-2 flux with the Xb47 and Xb55 ladder at a shared beam (Q3) to see whether Xb4f is itself low. (2) Interferometric CLEAN images with large negative bowls have a residual-scaling (JvM-type) uncertainty in the Jy/beam to flux conversion after beam-area rescaling. Add this to the systematic budget, along with the primary-beam correction at r=8-12 arcsec. (3) For Q1/Q4 and the non-LTE modelling, use single-array matched-beam ratios (Xb4d, or Xb4b smoothed) at N/S/Bridge. Add a 10-35% systematic whenever a high-resolution line is compared with a low-resolution one (e.g. ladder ratios built from Band 5/7 vs Band 6). Faint clumps need a 2x allowance.
